label: GO: lose-switch from a1 to a2
explanation: Fires only at GO (no D1/D2 activity) and on about 4% of GO steps. The strongest activations (near max) are on the agent switching from a1 to a2 after an unrewarded trial: the D1 input was reward 0, the previous choice was a1, and the policy now picks a2. 84% of activation mass is on GO steps where the model picks a2 and 72% where the previous reward was 0. The recorded predicate (prev reward 0, prev action a1, model picks a2) has dev precision 0.59, mass recall 0.47, and covers 60% of the top activation quartile. Part of the missed mass is at the first trial of the window, where prev_action is unknown in the data. The rest is weak, diffuse activation on other a2 choices, e.g. a2 stays after no reward, or GO steps that follow a rare transition. It is almost silent when the model picks a1 with high confidence (top choice-logit bin) and when the previous reward was 1 and the agent stays. Uses only observed variables plus the current choice of the agent (model_act at GO).
